purpose: Groundwork for the eventual commercial packaging split. Lists the entry points and HTTP routes that Round 6's settings audit flagged as CSRN-internal-only (release QA / dev tooling) and NOT appropriate for a customer build. DOCUMENTATION ONLY as of Round 7 -- nothing here is removed, gated, or restricted yet.
source: Round 6 Task A.6 + Round 7 Task C

entry_points.why: Second Flask entry point: application.run(host=CSRN_HOST, port=CSRN_PORT, debug=(CSRN_DEBUG=='1'), threaded=True). The real game-day launcher is app.py -> waitress.serve (no debug). A commercial build should ship only the waitress path.

route_blueprints.scope: partial -- this blueprint also serves customer routes (/api/state, /api/runtime-state, /api/config, /api/health). Only the diagnostics routes below are internal.
route_blueprints.why: Engine-status + live runtime diagnostics + incident-bundle export. Built for CSRN release QA; the operator does not need them to run a broadcast.
Pre-release drill tracking + release freeze/unfreeze + release manifest. This is CSRN's own release process, not broadcast operation.
route_blueprints.action_for_packaging: do not register in the commercial build

route_blueprints.scope: partial -- deployment + support-bundle are internal; the /api/licensing/* routes are CSRN licensing business (borderline; your call).
route_blueprints.why: Update packaging/validation and support-bundle generation are CSRN ops tooling. The support bundle in particular can collect logs/state and should not be a one-click customer action.

explicitly_not_listed.note: These were considered in Round 6 but are NOT classed internal-only here -- left for your decision.
items: recovery routes (/api/game-day/recovery/*) -- customer-relevant disaster recovery, advanced
upgrade module / upgrade_service -- customer-relevant if updates ship in-app
MHSAA import + DragonFly sync -- Mississippi/CSRN-specific data plumbing, not a debug surface
